subject: physics
question_text: What happens to the coefficient of friction if the weight of the body is doubled?

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 5 VERY SHORT ANSWER. The 1+1 mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for this question, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What doubles
lines: On a horizontal surface N = mg, so

lines.text: f = μN doubles along with it.

steps.margin_note: Show that BOTH f and N double. One of them alone proves nothing.
steps.why: The friction force really does double — that part of the student instinct is right. It is the RATIO that is being asked about.
common_mistakes: Answering that friction stays the same. The force doubles; only the coefficient does not.

recall.must_convey: That doubling the weight doubles the normal force and doubles the friction force with it.
accept: normal force doubles and friction doubles
N double aithe f kuda double avutundi

steps.label: What does not change

lines.text: μ = f / N does not change.

lines: μ depends only on the nature of the
steps.margin_note: Say what μ DOES depend on. That sentence is what separates a full answer from a bare "no change".
steps.why: Both numbers in the ratio are multiplied by two, so the ratio is untouched. μ is a property of the pair of surfaces, not of the load.
common_mistakes: Writing "μ doubles" from the fact that friction doubles.

recall.must_convey: That the coefficient of friction is unchanged, because it depends only on the surfaces.
accept: it depends only on the surfaces
mu marade, surfaces meeda depend avutundi
